questions.question: Which ancient Sanskrit text forms the basis of classical dance forms including Odissi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Natyashastra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Natyashastra** is a monumental ancient Indian treatise on the performing arts, traditionally credited to the legendary sage **Bharata Muni**. It serves as the primary technical and theoretical foundation for all **Indian classical dance** forms, including **Odissi**, **Bharatanatyam**, and **Kathakali**.
 
• Composed roughly between **200 BCE** and **200 CE**, it consists of **36 chapters** and over **6000 poetic verses**. It is often revered as the Panchama Veda&l

questions.question: Which physiographic division of India is geologically the oldest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Peninsular Plateau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Peninsular Plateau** is considered the oldest physiographic division of India, originating from the ancient supercontinent known as **Gondwanaland**.
 
• Geologically, it is a **stable shield** block composed of ancient **crystalline**, **igneous**, and **metamorphic rocks** that date back to the **Pre-Cambrian** era, making it far older than the **Himalayas**.
 
• The plateau was formed as a result of the breaking and drifting of the **Indian Plate** northward, eventually colliding with the **Eurasian Plate**.
 
• It covers a massive area of approximately **16 lakh square kilometers**, with an average elevation ranging between **600 to 900 meters** above sea level.
 
• The topography is characterized by **relict mountains** and **denuded hills** such as the **Aravallis**, which are among the oldest fold mountains in the world, further proving the geological antiquity of this region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himalayas**:

 
 
• These are classified as **Young Fold Mountains** that formed during the **Tertiary** period (approximately 40 to 50 million years ago) due to the **Alpine Orogeny**.
 
• They exhibit a high-relief topography with steep **V-shaped valleys** and **glaciers**, representing geological youth.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Gangetic Plains**:
 
 
• This region is an **aggradational plain** formed by the deposition of alluvium by the **Indus**, **Ganga**, and **Brahmaputra** rivers.
 
• It is the youngest physiographic division, belonging to the **Quaternary** period (Pleistocene and Holocene epochs).
 
 
 
• **Coastal Plains**:
 
 
• Divided into the **Western Coastal Plain** and **Eastern Coastal Plain**, these were formed by **marine deposits** and **fluvial activity**.
 
• The **Western Coast** is an example of a **submerged coastline**, whereas the **Eastern Coast** is characterized by **emergent** features and large deltas.

questions.question: Which temple is an example of the Kalinga style of architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jagannath Temple, Puri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jagannath Temple** in **Puri**, Odisha, is a premier example of **Kalinga Architecture**, which is a regional sub-style of the **Nagara** (North Indian) temple architecture style.
 
• Constructed in the **12th century**, the temple was commissioned by **King Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva**, the first monarch of the **Eastern Ganga Dynasty**.
 
• The temple complex follows a specific structural layout characteristic of the **Kalinga style**, comprising four main components: the **Vimana** (sanctum/Rekha Deula), the **Jagamohana** (assembly hall/Pidha Deula), the **Nata Mandira** (dance hall), and the **Bhoga Mandapa** (offering hall).
 
• It is famously known as the **White Pagoda** (to distinguish it from the **Konark Sun Temple** or Black Pagoda) and serves as one of the **Char Dham** pilgrimage sites for Hindus.
 
• The architecture is distinguished by its **curvilinear spire** (shikhara) and the absence of pillars in the main halls, a remarkable feat of **medieval engineering**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brihadeeswarar Temple**:

 
 
• Located in **Thanjavur**, it is a masterpiece of **Dravidian architecture** built by the **Chola King Raja Raja I**.
 
 
 
• **Meenakshi Temple**:
 
 
• Situated in **Madurai**, it represents the **Pandya** and **Nayaka** styles of **Dravidian architecture**, famous for its 14 towering **Gopurams**.
 
 
 
• **Shore Temple**:
 
 
• Located in **Mamallapuram**, it was built by the **Pallava Dynasty** under **Narasimhavarman II** and is one of the oldest structural stone temples in **South India**.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of clubs a golfer can carry during a round?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Rule 4.1b** of the official **Rules of Golf**, a player is strictly prohibited from carrying more than **14 clubs** during a competitive round.
 
• This regulation was formally adopted in **1938** by the **United States Golf Association (USGA)** and later by **The R&A** to prevent an arms race of equipment that was making the game less about skill and more about having a specialized club for every possible shot.
 
• Before this rule, it was not uncommon for professional golfers to carry as many as **20 to 30 clubs**, which also placed an immense physical burden on **caddies**.
 
• A player may start a round with fewer than 14 clubs and add more during the play until the **14-club limit** is reached, provided the additions do not cause an **undue delay** to the game.
 
• The selection of the 14 clubs is entirely up to the golfer, typically including a mix of **woods**, **irons**, **wedges**, and a **putter**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Penalty Framework**:

 
 
• In **Stroke Play**, the penalty for exceeding the limit is **two strokes** for each hole where a breach occurred, with a maximum penalty of **four strokes** per round.
 
• In **Match Play**, the penalty results in a **deduction of holes**, where the match score is adjusted by one hole for each hole the breach occurred, up to a maximum of **two holes**.
 
• Once a player discovers they have more than 14 clubs, they must immediately perform an **out-of-play procedure** to declare which clubs will not be used for the remainder of the round.
 
 
 
• **Equipment Evolution**:
 
 
• Modern players often swap clubs based on **course conditions**; for instance, replacing a **long iron** with a **hybrid** or adding a **60-degree lob wedge** depending on the speed of the greens and the thickness of the rough.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of non-ferrous minerals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They lack iron content**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-ferrous minerals** are a specific category of **metallic minerals** that do not contain **iron** (scientifically known as **ferrum**) as a significant component.
 
• The primary distinguishing factor of these minerals is their chemical composition, which makes them highly resistant to **corrosion** and **rusting**, unlike their ferrous counterparts.
 
• These minerals are characterized by physical properties such as high **malleability**, low weight, and exceptional **thermal and electrical conductivity**.
 
• Common examples found in the **Earth's crust** include **copper**, **lead**, **zinc**, **tin**, and precious metals like **gold** and **silver**. **Bauxite**, the ore used for **aluminum** production, is one of the most widely used non-ferrous minerals globally.
 
• From a geological perspective, they are often found in **igneous** and **metamorphic rock** formations, often extracted through **veins** and **lodes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ferrous Minerals**:

 
 
• These are metallic minerals that contain **iron** as a base element.
 
• They account for about **three-fourths** of the total value of the production of metallic minerals.
 
• Major examples include **iron ore**, **manganese**, **chromite**, and **pyrite**.
 
• They are essential for the development of the **metallurgical industries** and the manufacturing of **steel**.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Applications**:
 
 
• Because they **lack iron content**, non-ferrous minerals are vital in **aeronautical**, **electrical**, and **engineering** industries.
 
• **Copper** is indispensable in the **power industry** for cables and electronics, while **aluminum** is favored in **automobile** and **packaging** sectors due to its strength-to-weight ratio.

questions.question: The third volume of the Akbar Nama is known as which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ain-i-Akbari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Akbar Nama** (Book of Akbar) is the official chronicle of the reign of **Akbar**, the third **Mughal Emperor**, written in the **Persian language**.
 
• It was authored by **Abul Fazl**, one of the **Navaratnas** (nine gems) and the court historian in **Akbar's court**.
 
• The work is organized into three distinct volumes: the first deals with **Akbar's ancestors**, the second records the events of **Akbar's reign** up to 1602, and the third is the **Ain-i-Akbari**.
 
• The **Ain-i-Akbari** serves as a detailed **administrative gazetteer**, providing exhaustive information about the **Mughal Empire's** governance, **army**, **revenue system**, and **geography**.
 
• It is further divided into five books (daftars), covering everything from the **imperial household** and **civil administration** to **Indian philosophy** and customs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tuzuk-i-Baburi**:

 
 
• This is the **autobiography** of the founder of the Mughal Empire, **Babur**.
 
• Unlike later official histories written in Persian, it was originally written in **Chaghatai Turkic** and later translated into Persian as the **Baburnama**.
 
 
 
• **Razmnama**:
 
 
• This term translates to the 'Book of War' and is the **Persian translation** of the ancient Indian epic, the **Mahabharata**.
 
• It was commissioned by **Akbar** to encourage **religious tolerance** and cultural exchange between the various communities of the empire.
 
 
 
• **Fatwa-i-Jahandari**:
 
 
• A significant work on **political philosophy** and statecraft written by **Ziauddin Barani**.
 
• It dates back to the **Delhi Sultanate** period and outlines the duties and ideals of a Muslim ruler in India.

questions.question: As of May 2025, who occupies the position of Chairman of the Bar Council of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manan Kumar Mishra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Manan Kumar Mishra**, a **Senior Advocate** originally from the state of **Bihar**, has held the prestigious position of **Chairman of the Bar Council of India (BCI)** for several consecutive terms, representing a significant period of leadership in the Indian legal regulatory framework.
 
• The **Bar Council of India** is a **statutory body** created by Parliament under **Section 4** of the **Advocates Act, 1961**, to regulate and represent the Indian Bar.
 
• As Chairman, the individual is responsible for presiding over meetings that determine **legal education standards**, **professional ethics**, and the **disciplinary jurisdiction** over advocates in India.
 
• The **Bar Council of India** consists of members elected from each **State Bar Council**, and the **Chairman** and **Vice-Chairman** are elected by these members from among themselves for a specific term.
 
• Under his tenure, the BCI has focused on mandatory **All India Bar Examination (AIBE)** reforms and the regulation of foreign law firms entering the Indian market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bar Council of India (BCI)**:

 
 
• **Functions**: It sets the standards of **professional conduct** and etiquette for advocates and establishes the curriculum for **Law Degrees** in recognized universities.
 
• **Ex-officio Members**: The **Attorney General of India** and the **Solicitor General of India** serve as ex-officio members of the Council.
 
• **Legal Education Committee**: The BCI includes a committee that visits and inspects **Universities** to ensure compliance with its educational guidelines.
 
 
 
• **Distinction from SCBA**:
 
 
• It is important to distinguish the **Bar Council of India** from the **Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA)**. While the BCI is a statutory regulatory body for all advocates, the SCBA is a voluntary bar association for practitioners specifically in the **Supreme Court of India**.
 
• Individuals like **Vikas Singh** and **Dushyant Dave** have historically served as the **President** of the **Supreme Court Bar Association**, which is an elected post distinct from the statutory BCI chairmanship.

questions.question: In November 2024, who has been appointed as Chairman at Indian Oil Corporation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arvinder Singh Sahney**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **November 2024**, the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)** officially approved the appointment of **Arvinder Singh Sahney** as the **Chairman** of the **Indian Oil Corporation (IOCL)**.
 
• Prior to this top-tier leadership role, **Sahney** served as the **Executive Director (Business Development - Petrochemicals)** at the company’s corporate headquarters, where he played a crucial role in expanding the **petrochemicals** portfolio.
 
• The **Public Enterprises Selection Board (PESB)** had recommended his name for the post in **August 2024**, following a rigorous selection process to fill the vacancy left by the previous permanent head.
 
• With a professional career spanning over **three decades**, he possesses extensive expertise in **refinery operations**, **supply chain management**, and the **execution of large-scale projects** within the **hydrocarbon sector**.
 
• His appointment is significant as he takes charge of India’s largest **commercial enterprise** at a time when the company is focusing on **energy transition** and achieving **net-zero operational emissions** by **2046**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL)**:

 
 
• It is a **Maharatna** Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE) established in **1959** and headquartered in **New Delhi**.
 
• It functions under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas**, Government of India.
 
• The corporation is the highest-ranked **Indian energy PSU** in the **Fortune Global 500** list and controls nearly half of India’s **petroleum products market share**.
 
• IOCL operates a massive network of **refineries** (including **Digboi**, **Mathura**, and **Paradip**), **pipelines** for crude and product transport, and thousands of **fuel stations** across the country.
 
• The company is also a leader in **liquefied petroleum gas (LPG)** marketing through the **Indane** brand, serving millions of households.

questions.question: As of July 2025, more than ____ Anganwadi Centres have been upgraded into Saksham Anganwadi Centres.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**87661**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0** is a flagship program of the **Ministry of Women and Child Development** designed to tackle malnutrition and enhance early childhood development across India.
 
• A primary objective of this mission is the phased upgrading of **2 lakh Anganwadi Centres** into **Saksham Anganwadi Centres**, aiming for a transformation of approximately 40,000 centers annually.
 
• As of the data recorded in **July 2025**, the government has successfully upgraded a total of **87,661** centres, marking a significant step toward achieving the comprehensive five-year target (2021-22 to 2025-26).
 
• These upgraded centers serve as modernized hubs that integrate **Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE)** with improved nutritional support for children, pregnant women, and lactating mothers.
 
• The transition to **Saksham** status involves significant investments in infrastructure, ensuring that basic amenities like **clean drinking water**, **functional toilets**, and **internal electrification** are prioritized.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Core Features of Saksham Anganwadis:
 
 
• **Digital Infrastructure**: These centers are equipped with **smart learning aids**, **LED screens**, and high-speed **internet/Wi-Fi connectivity** to support interactive pedagogical methods.
 
• **Nutritional Monitoring**: Utilization of the **Poshan Tracker** application for real-time monitoring of growth and nutritional status through digitized records.
 
• **Eco-friendly Initiatives**: Many centers incorporate **Rainwater Harvesting** systems and **Solar Power** units to promote environmental sustainability and reduce operational costs.
 
 
 
• **Mission Poshan 2.0** Strategy:
 
 
• Focuses on **maternal nutrition**, **infant and young child feeding norms**, and the treatment of **Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM)** and **Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM)**.
 
• Promotes the establishment of **Poshan Vatikas** (nutrition gardens) to provide fresh, local produce and encourage the consumption of **millets** and traditional foods.
 
• Ensures convergence with other national schemes like the **Jal Jeevan Mission** for providing tap water connections to every Anganwadi.

questions.question: Who is the Chairman of Zonal Councils in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Union Home Minister**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zonal Councils** are **statutory bodies** and not constitutional bodies, established under **Part III of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956**.
 
• The **Union Home Minister** acts as the **ex-officio Chairman** for all five Zonal Councils in India, ensuring a unified approach to regional issues.
 
• These councils are deliberative and **advisory bodies** intended to promote **inter-state cooperation** and coordination on matters like **socio-economic planning**, **border disputes**, and **linguistic minorities**.
 
• The structure includes the **Chairman**, the **Chief Ministers** of the states in the zone, and **two other ministers** from each state nominated by the Governor.
 
• The **States Reorganisation Act, 1956** divided the country into five zones: **Northern**, **Central**, **Eastern**, **Western**, and **Southern**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Internal Organization and Roles**:

 
 
• The **Chief Ministers** of the states within the zone act as the **Vice-Chairman** of the respective council by **rotation**, holding the office for **one year** at a time.
 
• The **Chief Secretary** of each state and another officer from the state act as **advisers** to the council.
 
• The **North-Eastern Council** was created under a separate legislation called the **North-Eastern Council Act, 1971**, to address the specific needs of states like **Assam**, **Manipur**, and **Sikkim**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Bodies**:
 
 
• The **Prime Minister** is the Chairman of the **Inter-State Council** (established under **Article 263** of the Constitution) and the **NITI Aayog**.
 
• The **Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog** is an administrative head of the think tank and does not preside over Zonal Councils.
 
• The **President** of India appoints the members of the **Inter-State Council** but does not chair the Zonal Councils.

questions.question: Which Indian state is establishing world's first black tiger safari?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The state government of **Odisha** officially announced the setting up of the **world’s first melanistic tiger safari** near the **Similipal Tiger Reserve (STR)** in **Mayurbhanj** district.
 
• This ambitious project is being established near **Baripada**, covering an expansive area of about **200 hectares**, designed to provide a habitat for **black tigers** that are either surplus from zoos or unfit for the wild.
 
• **Similipal Tiger Reserve** is unique globally as it is the only natural habitat that hosts a wild population of **melanistic tigers**, which are characterized by thick, fused **black stripes** due to a rare genetic mutation.
 
• The initiative received in-principle approval from the **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)** and the **Central Zoo Authority (CZA)** to promote **wildlife tourism** and spread awareness about this rare feline variant.
 
• The **melanism** in these tigers is linked to a mutation in the **Taqpep gene**, a discovery made by researchers to explain why the stripes are exceptionally broad and dark, often hiding the tawny background fur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Similipal Tiger Reserve**:

 
 
• It was formally designated a **Tiger Reserve** in **1973** and became part of the **UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves** in **2009**.
 
• The reserve is a critical part of the **Mayurbhanj Elephant Reserve** and houses diverse fauna, including the **Asian Elephant** and **Chausingha**.
 
 
 
• **Melanistic Tiger Population**:
 
 
• According to the **All India Tiger Estimation 2022**, approximately **10 melanistic tigers** were identified within the **Similipal** landscape.
 
• The prevalence of these tigers in **Odisha** is attributed to **genetic isolation** and **inbreeding** within a small population, leading to the manifestation of recessive traits.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding New Space India Limited?

I. It is a private sector enterprise.

II. It involved in the construction and in-orbit delivery of various types and classes of satellites.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **New Space India Limited (NSIL)** was incorporated on **6 March 2019** as a **Wholly Owned Government of India Company**. It is a **Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE)** under the administrative control of the **Department of Space (DoS)** and the **Companies Act, 2013**. It is not a private sector enterprise but a commercial arm of the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**. ***Hence, statement I is incorrect.***
 
• The primary mandate of **NSIL** involves a **demand-driven model** where it takes responsibility for the **construction**, **assembly**, **integration**, and **in-orbit delivery** of various types and classes of satellites. This includes managing satellite missions and providing launch services for both domestic and international customers using **ISRO** launch vehicles. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **New Space India Limited (NSIL)**:

 
 
• **Headquarters**: The organization is headquartered in **Bengaluru**, Karnataka.
 
• **Mission**: Its goal is to enable Indian industries to scale up high-technology manufacturing and to commercialize products and services emanating from the **Indian Space Programme**.
 
• **Production Mandate**: **NSIL** is responsible for the production of **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicles (PSLV)** and **Small Satellite Launch Vehicles (SSLV)** through industrial consortia.
 
• **Technology Transfer**: It acts as the nodal agency for the **transfer of technology (ToT)** from **ISRO** to the Indian private industry for various space-related applications.
 
• **Satellite Communication**: It is also involved in providing **satellite-based services** like transponder leasing and mission support for Earth observation and communication satellites.

questions.question: In December 2024, which institute developed a low-cost 'tinnitus device' with a mobile solution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IIT Bombay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **December 2024**, researchers at the **Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (IIT Bombay)** designed and developed an innovative, **low-cost tinnitus management device** integrated with a **smartphone-based mobile application**.
 
• **Tinnitus** is a neurological and audiological condition characterized by a persistent ringing, buzzing, or hissing sound in the ears without any external acoustic stimulus.
 
• The newly developed device works on the principle of **acoustic neuromodulation**, utilizing tailored sound frequencies to retrain the brain's auditory cortex and reduce the perception of tinnitus.
 
• By pairing the wearable hardware with a customized **mobile solution**, this technology delivers personalized sound therapy, significantly lowering treatment costs and enhancing patient accessibility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tinnitus Therapeutics**:

 
 
• Conventional white-noise generators and customized sound-masking devices are often expensive and imported, making this **indigenous development** highly critical for affordable healthcare in India.
 
 
 
• **Other Premier Institutions**:
 
 
• **IISc Bengaluru**: Renowned for its cutting-edge research in **nanotechnology**, **aerospace engineering**, and foundational sciences.
 
• **IIT Kanpur**: Highly active in bioengineering, famously developing artificial hearts, and advanced **cybersecurity systems**.
 
• **JIPMER Puducherry**: A premier medical institution focused on **clinical healthcare**, medical education, and public health research.

questions.question: The 17th BRICS summit was held at ___.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rio de Janeiro**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **17th BRICS Summit** is scheduled to be hosted by **Brazil** in **2025**, following the group's established tradition of rotating the chairmanship annually among member nations.
 
• **Rio de Janeiro** has been designated as the host city for this high-level diplomatic event, which will bring together leaders from the expanded **BRICS+** alliance.
 
• The summit represents a critical milestone for **Brazil** as it assumes the leadership role to facilitate discussions on **global governance reform**, **sustainable development**, and **financial cooperation**.
 
• This meeting will be the second summit following the historic expansion of the bloc in **2024**, which saw nations like **Egypt**, **Ethiopia**, **Iran**, and the **United Arab Emirates** join the founding members.
 
• The **Rio de Janeiro** summit is expected to focus heavily on the **de-dollarization** of trade and the strengthening of the **New Development Bank (NDB)** to support infrastructure in the Global South.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kaizen**:

 
 
• A **Japanese philosophy** and business concept that translates to **continuous improvement**.
 
• It involves all employees from the CEO to assembly line workers to improve all functions and processes within an organization.
 
 
 
• **Shanghai**:
 
 
• A major financial hub in **China** that serves as the permanent headquarters for the **New Development Bank (NDB)**.
 
• It is a central location for **BRICS** financial policy coordination and economic research.
 
 
 
• **Vladivostok**:
 
 
• A strategic port city in **Russia** that hosts the annual **Eastern Economic Forum (EEF)**.
 
• While a key site for **Eurasian** diplomacy, it is not the venue for the 17th BRICS gathering.
 
 
 
• **16th BRICS Summit**:
 
 
• Held in **Kazan**, Russia, in October **2024**, focusing on the integration of new member states into the bloc's framework.

questions.question: 'Tingtang', a traditional Mizo instrument, is known as the Mizo version of which instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Guitar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tingtang** is a traditional **stringed instrument** originating from the **Mizo** tribe of **Mizoram**, widely regarded as the indigenous version of the **Guitar**.
 
• It is scientifically classified as a **plucked chordophone**, where melodic sound is produced by vibrating strings stretched over a **hollow resonator**.
 
• The instrument is traditionally crafted using a **hollowed block of wood** or **bamboo** as the soundbox, which provides the necessary **acoustic resonance** for performance.
 
• Historically, the **Tingtang** featured **single or multiple strings** made of **animal gut** or wire, allowing the player to pluck them while varying the pitch, similar to the functionality of a **lute** or guitar.
 
• In **Mizo folk music**, this instrument is primarily used to accompany **oral storytelling** and folk songs, bridging the gap between ancient rhythmic patterns and modern **melodic structures**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other Traditional Instruments of **Mizoram**:

 
 
• **Khuang**: The most significant **Mizo percussion instrument**, equivalent to a **Drum**, made from a hollowed tree trunk and **cowhide**; it is indispensable during the **Cheraw** dance.
 
• **Tuium**: A type of **bamboo flute** representing the **wind instrument** category, used to produce soft and mellow tunes.
 
• **Dar**: These are **brass gongs** or **cymbals** used in sets to provide **rhythmic timing** during major festivals like **Chapchar Kut**.
 
• **Rawchhem**: A unique **Mizo wind instrument** made of **bamboo tubes** and a **dried gourd**, operating on a principle similar to a **bagpipe** or **harmonica**.

questions.question: Pratibha Devisingh Patil assumed office as the ____ President of India on July 25, 2007.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pratibha Devisingh Patil** served as the **12th President of India**, holding the highest constitutional office from **July 25, 2007**, to **July 25, 2012**.
 
• She made history by becoming the **first woman** to serve as the President of the Republic of India since the office was established in 1950.
 
• She succeeded **Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam**, who was the **11th President**, and was later succeeded by **Pranab Mukherjee**, the 13th President.
 
• During the **2007 Presidential Election**, she was the candidate of the **United Progressive Alliance (UPA)** and defeated the then Vice-President **Bhairon Singh Shekhawat**.
 
• Prior to her tenure as President, she served as the **Governor of Rajasthan** from 2004 to 2007, also becoming the first woman to hold that position in the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ramaswamy Venkataraman**

 
 
• Served as the **8th President of India** (1987–1992).
 
• He previously held the office of the **Vice-President** and worked as the **Union Minister of Finance** and **Minister of Defence**.
 
 
 
• **K.R. Narayanan**
 
 
• Served as the **10th President of India** (1997–2002).
 
• He was the first member of the **Dalit community** to hold the post of President and Vice-President.
 
 
 
• **Ram Nath Kovind**
 
 
• Served as the **14th President of India** (2017–2022).
 
• Before his presidency, he served as the **Governor of Bihar** and was a member of the **Rajya Sabha**.

questions.question: How many total categories which are used for assessment in Performance Grading Index (PGI) 2.0 (by Ministry of Education)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Performance Grading Index (PGI) 2.0** is a specialized tool launched by the **Department of School Education and Literacy**, **Ministry of Education**, to evaluate the performance of the school education system across all States and Union Territories in India.
 
• The updated framework of **PGI 2.0** is built upon a total weightage of **1,000 points**, which are distributed across **73 indicators**.
 
• These indicators are fundamentally organized into **two primary categories**: **Outcomes** and **Governance Management**.
 
• The **Outcomes** category is designed to measure the actual results of the education process, including student performance and system reach.
 
• The **Governance Management** category focuses on the institutional framework, administrative efficiency, and the digital interventions used to manage the education system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structure of Domains**:

 
 
• Within the **two broad categories**, the index is further subdivided into **six domains**.
 
• These domains include **Learning Outcomes**, **Access**, **Infrastructure & Facilities**, **Equity**, **Governance Process**, and **Teacher Education and Training**.
 
 
 
• **Grading System**:
 
 
• **PGI 2.0** does not rank states but classifies them into **ten specific grades**.
 
• The highest grade is **Daksh** (for scores above 940), followed by **Utkarsh**, **Ati-Uttam**, **Uttam**, **Prachesta-1**, **Prachesta-2**, **Prachesta-3**, **Akanshi-1**, **Akanshi-2**, and the lowest being **Akanshi-3** (for scores up to 460).
 
 
 
• **Evolution of PGI**:
 
 
• The original **PGI** (1.0) was first released for the year **2017-18**. **PGI 2.0** was introduced to align the indicators with the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020** and to ensure more robust data-driven monitoring.

questions.question: As per SIPRI report published in March 2025, which of the following countries is NOT one of the top 5 arms importers between in 2020-24?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**North Korea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI)** released its report in **March 2025**, analyzing international arms transfers during the period **2020-24**.
 
• According to the data, **India** maintained its position as the world's **largest arms importer**, accounting for approximately **9% to 10%** of total global arms imports during this five-year block.
 
• **Ukraine** rose significantly in the rankings to become the **second-largest arms importer** in the world, a direct consequence of military assistance and procurement following the **Russian invasion**.
 
• **Pakistan** also featured within the **top 5 arms importers** globally, driven by its ongoing military modernization programs and strategic partnerships, primarily with **China**.
 
• The other nations typically rounding out the top 5 in this period include **Saudi Arabia** and **Qatar**, making the **Middle East** and **Asia** the primary destination regions for major conventional weapons.
 
• **North Korea** is not included in the top 5 list as it is under stringent **United Nations Security Council sanctions** that prohibit the international trade of arms, and it does not engage in transparent, large-scale legal arms imports monitored by **SIPRI**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Detailed Importer Profiles (2020-24):**

 
 
• **India:** Its primary suppliers remained **Russia**, **France**, and the **USA**, though the share of Russian imports has seen a gradual decline in favor of **indigenization** and Western diversification.
 
• **Ukraine:** The massive influx of arms was characterized by **high-tech surveillance**, **air defense systems**, and **armored vehicles** supplied by over 30 states.
 
• **Pakistan:** Occupies a high rank due to its role as a major recipient of **Chinese combat aircraft** and **naval vessels**.
 
• **Global Trends:** The **SIPRI 2025** report highlights that while global arms trade volumes fluctuated, the **United States** and **France** increased their exports, whereas **Russia's** exports dropped significantly.
 
• **SIPRI:** Founded in **1966** in **Stockholm**, it is an independent international institute dedicated to research into conflict, armaments, arms control, and **disarmament**.
